title: What does a folded sheet with paint show when opened?
description: A sheet is folded in half, paint is spilled on one half, and the halves are pressed together. The opened sheet shows the same shape on both sides of the crease, and only the crease makes the halves cover each other. Keeko's doubt is that the pattern can be folded along lots of lines.
teaching_notes: One idea: pressing paint from one folded half prints a mirror picture, so the crease is a line of symmetry. Watch for students who think any fold line of a spilled pattern works.

source: Take a piece of paper and fold it in half. Open it and spill
video_script.why: The child sees that a folded print is a mirror picture, so the crease is a line of symmetry, and a spilled pattern has only that one.
video_script.substitution: Fold, press and open: the crease is the mirror between the two matching halves.
video_script.anchor: a sheet of paper folded in half, with a few drops of paint on one half
video_script.wrong_answer: the pattern can be folded along lots of lines
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the pattern can be folded along lots of lines, because the paint is everywhere. Folding the sheet across the other way shows the halves do not match, so only the crease works.
video_script.payoff_line: The pattern is symmetric, and the crease is its only line of symmetry

final_answer.value: Yes, symmetric; the crease is the line of symmetry; no other line works
final_answer.spoken: the pattern is the same on both sides, and the crease is its only line of symmetry

names.Leeza: the Class 5 activity of pressing a paint pattern between folded halves

maths_rules: Fold in half: the crease is a straight line down the middle
Paint on one half presses onto the other half and prints a mirror image, so the two halves match when folded
The crease is a line of symmetry because the halves cover each other exactly
A spilled pattern does not match on both sides of any other fold line, so it has just the one line of symmetry
video_script.design: One idea: fold, press and open prints a mirror picture, so the crease is the line of symmetry. The anchor sheet stays all video. Wrong idea: any fold line works for a spilled pattern.
